questions.stem: The number of water molecules in $9\ \text{g}$ of water is ($N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$)

options.whyWrong: This is one mole. 9 g of water is only half a mole.
The mass (9) was multiplied by $N_A$ without converting to moles.
This is the number of *atoms* (3 per molecule).

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** moles first, then multiply by $N_A$.

1. $n = 9/18 = 0.5\ \text{mol}$
2. $N = 0.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} =$ **$3.011 \times 10^{23}$**
hints: Molar mass of water is 18 g/mol.
